public_rationale: The categorical attribution is contradicted by the essay. Sutton argues that scalable general methods ultimately prevail, while acknowledging initial improvements from incorporating human knowledge. That is different from saying progress has always come from scaling and never from hand engineering. Marcus's broader opinion that the essay overstates its historical lesson remains a separate question.
limitations: The result concerns the factual attribution in the exact words, not a comprehensive verdict on Marcus's criticism of scaling.
A reading restricted to long-run breakthroughs would require a different historical assessment.
The source is an institutional reproduction of the original essay.

A thesis about which methods ultimately dominate is weaker than a claim about the source of all progress.
